content.text: I'll plan the cathedral's subsystems first, then build west front, nave, buttresses, and spire in stages.
Dark plinth first.
West front block: 20×6 ring, 12 courses, three portals and a rose opening.
Towers rising above with tall belfry openings on all four faces.
Stained glass in the rose opening — mixed trans bricks with rounded corners.
Nave body: 10×32 walls, ten courses, tall window openings both sides.
Glass panels for the eight nave windows, on interior support columns.
Those landed on the wall top, not in the openings — removing and re-seating them properly.
Roof: stepped black slope courses starting at the eaves. Testing orientation first.
Deck and stepped black roof courses with a ridge.
Flying buttresses: ten piers with stepped struts and pinnacles.
Spire at the crossing, rising above the towers.
Tower top cornices and corner pinnacles.
Facade balustrade and a stepped parvis in front of the portals.
Tying the separate structures together.
Apse at the east end, with a glowing east window.
Dark recessed portals with tympanum bands.
Those stacked on top of the facade — removing them.
Portal infill with 2×3 bricks seated on the floor.
Those stacked on top again — removing, then seating the fill on the floor plate.
